question: Can machine-learning systems be designed to support users' autonomous growth and flourishing rather than maximize revealed preferences or engagement?

key_findings.claim: Maslow's Gridworld demonstrates by construction how high-salience, low-need-replenishment stimuli decouple observed engagement from the paper's stipulated flourishing measure.
key_findings.evidence: A fixed policy repeatedly chooses salient belonging cells; adversarial cells significantly reduce average needs met relative to a supportive environment (p<1e-5 over reported runs), and evolutionary optimization for engagement converges toward more such cells.

key_findings.claim: The proposed machine-love framework operationalizes practical loving action as care, responsibility, respect, and knowledge while explicitly rejecting simulated affect as necessary.
key_findings.evidence: Adapted from Fromm, care concerns active support for growth, responsibility supplies channels to respond, respect centers user autonomy, and knowledge means an increasingly deep model of the person's aspirations and obstacles.

key_findings.claim: Prompted text-davinci-003 can classify the paper's simulated flourishing narratives and use dialogue to correct a population prior for users with different experiences.
key_findings.evidence: A care prompt distinguishes supportive from adversarial gridworld logs; a conversational respect condition distinguishes simulated addictive versus enriching social-media use with Fisher's exact p<0.0001, whereas the naive prior misclassifies enriching users.

key_findings.claim: The attachment-theory demonstration tests model-generated personas rather than people, so its high scores establish internal simulation consistency, not clinical validity or benefit.
key_findings.evidence: After four synthetic relationship logs at a 95% confidence threshold, the system makes no errors across ten anxious/avoidant and secure/secure simulations and detects scripted contempt at 99.6%; the resulting gridworld app accelerates a hand-coded self-awareness transition.

method.core_idea: Replace a single preference proxy with a plural, autonomy-sensitive framework for actions that support growth, and prototype its components using language-model judgments in a toy environment.
method.mechanism: Construct a Maslow-inspired need-decay gridworld, evolve environments for engagement or flourishing, translate trajectories into text, prompt text-davinci-003 to assess growth or interview simulated personas, and add scripted attachment dynamics to test personalized psychological inference.
assumptions: Maslow's hierarchy is a useful toy ground truth for flourishing despite acknowledged controversy.
LLM simulation of user narratives provides meaningful proof-of-concept evidence for human-facing inference.
Fromm's four principles can be abstracted into operational machine behaviors.
Plural qualitative principles resist proxy gaming better than a single engagement measure.

techniques.role: Makes engagement-flourishing divergence explicit under engineered salience.
Structures assistance around care, response capability, autonomy, and personalized knowledge.
Uses an LM's psychological prior to evaluate textualized behavior logs.
Allows simulated self-report to override a generic wellbeing prior.

evaluations.setting: Supportive versus adversarial Maslow gridworld over 40 reported runs
evaluations.metric: Average need level met and engagement
evaluations.result: Adversarial high-salience/low-replenishment cells reduce stipulated flourishing with p<1e-5
evaluations.baseline: Supportive cells whose salience tracks replenishment

evaluations.result: Engagement optimization eventually lowers flourishing; flourishing optimization raises both in the toy model

evaluations.setting: LM dialogue with addictive-responding and growth-responding simulated social-media users
evaluations.result: Conversational condition distinguishes personas with Fisher's exact p<0.0001
evaluations.baseline: Naive care prior based only on behavior

evaluations.result: No reported errors after four logs at 95% threshold for selected pairings; 99.6% contempt classification
evaluations.baseline: Hand-scripted persona labels and relational cycle

limitations: Author-stated: all user evidence comes from language-model simulations rather than human studies.
Maslow's hierarchy, Fromm's account, and attachment categories are contestable cultural and psychological simplifications.
The same model generates personas and evaluates their logs, allowing shared-prompt artifacts and circular validation.
No intervention is tested for durable human wellbeing, autonomy, dependency, privacy, or clinical harm.
Psychological personalization can enable manipulation, paternalism, surveillance, and reward gaming at scale.
failure_modes: A flourishing proxy becomes gamed just as engagement does.
The system mistakes culturally normative or personally meaningful behavior for pathology.
Users defer to confident but false psychological labels, changing relationships or treatment decisions.
Simulated empathy encourages emotional dependency despite the framework's stated non-relational goal.
Sensitive behavioral histories are repurposed for persuasion or commercial targeting.
reusable_insights: Let explicit, revisable user feedback override generic population priors about wellbeing.
Treat autonomy and opt-out as first-class outcomes, not constraints added after optimization.
Validate psychological assistance with independent human studies and adverse-event monitoring, never self-simulated personas alone.
open_questions: What consented human-subject protocol can test benefit without creating dependency or pseudo-clinical authority?
How can users inspect, correct, delete, and locally control inferred psychological profiles?
Can plural principles be evaluated for long-term flourishing without collapsing into a gameable scalar?

competitive_landscape.title: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: CIRL models a robot uncertain about a human reward and derives cooperative information-seeking behavior; Machine Love challenges fixed revealed preferences more radically with qualitative growth principles but lacks comparable formal guarantees.

competitive_landscape.title: Multi-Principal Assistance Games: Definition and Collegial Mechanisms
competitive_landscape.difference: Multi-principal games formalize aggregation and strategic preference revelation among many humans; Machine Love advocates multiple culturally local implementations but does not solve aggregation or institutional power.

competitive_landscape.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
competitive_landscape.difference: Constitutional AI trains assistants against an explicit rule set and evaluates harmlessness; Machine Love proposes a richer wellbeing-oriented constitution but demonstrates it only through prompting in simulations.

competitive_landscape.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
competitive_landscape.difference: Generative Agents evaluate memory, reflection, and behavior in interactive simulacra; Machine Love uses simulated persons as stand-ins for psychological intervention evidence, raising an even stronger need for independent human validation.

novelty_assessment: The paper is a provocative design agenda and a useful warning against equating engagement with welfare. Its four-principle framework is conceptually generative, but the experiments are engineered demonstrations with circular LM personas and stipulated flourishing; they do not establish safe psychological inference or real human benefit.
reviewer_notes: Read the full argument, gridworld mechanics, LM prompt experiments, attachment simulation, and extensive ethical-limitations sections. Primary arXiv records on assistance games, constitutional AI, and LM simulacra were checked on 2026-08-23.
